html:
A strong earthquake struck Constantinople and the lands around the Sea of Marmara on 26 October 740. It brought down stretches of the land walls, many churches and houses, and damaged towns in Thrace and Bithynia, including Nicomedia.

Emperor Leo III raised taxes to repair the walls, and inscriptions naming him and his son Constantine V can still be seen on them. The church of Hagia Irene, beside Hagia Sophia, was badly damaged and rebuilt under Constantine V. Its apse holds a large plain cross instead of a picture of Christ or Mary, a well known example of church decoration from the age of iconoclasm. The quake struck in the last year of Leo's reign.
